        return $true
    }

    $rows = @($failing | Sort-Object { [string]$_.displayName } | ForEach-Object {
            [pscustomobject][ordered]@{ PreStage = [string]$_.displayName; Mandatory = [bool]$_.mandatory; 'MDM profile removable' = [bool]$_.mdmRemovable }
        })
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "$($failing.Count) of $($prestages.Count) computer PreStage enrollments let a user skip enrollment or remove the MDM profile, which takes the Mac out of management.`n`n$(ConvertTo-JamfMarkdownTable -InputObject $rows)"
    $false
}
--- md
A computer PreStage enrollment sets how a Mac from Apple Business Manager or Apple School Manager enrolls in Jamf
Pro during Setup Assistant. When enrollment is not mandatory, the user can skip it. When the MDM profile is
removable, any user can remove it in System Settings, and the Mac loses every configuration profile, restriction
and security setting that Jamf Pro manages.

This test reads every computer PreStage enrollment and fails when one does not make the MDM profile mandatory or
allows it to be removed. It supports NIST SP 800-53 CM-6 (configuration settings) and AC-19 (access control for
mobile devices).

#### Remediation action

1. In Jamf Pro, go to **Computers** > **PreStage Enrollments** and open each PreStage enrollment this test lists.
2. Click **Edit**, and on the **General** payload select **Make MDM Profile Mandatory** and clear **Allow MDM
   Profile Removal**.
3. Click **Save**. The change applies to Macs that enroll from then on; re-enroll existing Macs through Setup
   Assistant to apply it to them.

- [Jamf Pro documentation: Computer PreStage Enrollments](https://learn.jamf.com/r/en-US/jamf-pro-documentation-current/Computer_PreStage_Enrollments)
- [Jamf Pro API: GET /v3/computer-prestages](https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v3-computer-prestages)

authentication, anyone who has the Mac, such as a person who finds or steals it before it is set up, gets a managed

their directory or single sign-on account during enrollment. It supports NIST SP 800-53 IA-2 (identification and
authentication of users) and AC-19 (access control for mobile devices).

    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that every enabled Jamf Pro webhook sends its events over HTTPS and authenticates to the receiving server.
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id                 = 'MP.JAMF.1017',
        Title              = 'Webhooks send over HTTPS with authentication',
        Product            = 'Jamf Pro',
        Feature            = 'Webhooks',
        Area               = 'data-protection',
        ResourceType       = 'Connector',
        Severity           = 'Low',
        UserImpact         = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre              = ('T1557', 'T1040'),
        Control            = 'nist-800-53-r5:SC-8',
        Service            = 'JAMF.JamfPro',
        Author             = 'merill'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # Names of webhooks that may send without HTTPS or authentication, such as one to a server on the same host.
        [string[]] $ExcludedWebhook = @()
    )

    $list = Invoke-JamfProRequest -Path 'JSSResource/webhooks'
    # The Classic API answers { "webhooks": [ { id, name } ] }; older servers nest the list in "webhook".
    $entries = @($list.webhooks | Where-Object { $null -ne $_ })
    if ($entries.Count -eq 1 -and $entries[0].PSObject.Properties['webhook']) { $entries = @($entries[0].webhook | Where-Object { $null -ne $_ }) }
    if ($entries.Count -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason 'Jamf Pro has no webhook.'
        return
    }

    $checked = 0
    $failing = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
    foreach ($entry in $entries) {
        $answer = Invoke-JamfProRequest -Path "JSSResource/webhooks/id/$([int]$entry.id)"
        $webhook = if ($answer.PSObject.Properties['webhook']) { $answer.webhook } else { $answer }
        if ([string]$webhook.enabled -ne 'true' -or [string]$webhook.name -in $ExcludedWebhook) { continue }
        $checked++

        $uri = $null
        $https = [uri]::TryCreate([string]$webhook.url, [System.UriKind]::Absolute, [ref] $uri) -and $uri.Scheme -eq 'https'
        $authentication = if ($webhook.authentication_type) { [string]$webhook.authentication_type } else { 'NONE' }
        if ($https -and $authentication -ne 'NONE') { continue }

        # Only the scheme and host: a webhook address can carry a secret in its path or query. The password is never read.
        $server = if ($uri) { "$($uri.Scheme)://$($uri.Host)" } else { 'Not a valid address' }
        $failing.Add([pscustomobject][ordered]@{
                Webhook        = [string]$webhook.name
                Event          = [string]$webhook.event
                Server         = $server
                HTTPS          = $https
                Authentication = $authentication
            })
    }

    if ($checked -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason 'Jamf Pro has no enabled webhook that this test checks.'
        return
    }
    if ($failing.Count -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "Well done. All $checked enabled webhooks send over HTTPS and authenticate to the receiving server."
        return $true
    }

    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "$($failing.Count) of $checked enabled webhooks send without HTTPS or without authentication. Their events, which name devices, users and changes, can be read on the network, and the receiving server cannot tell them from forged ones.`n`n$(ConvertTo-JamfMarkdownTable -InputObject @($failing))"
    $false
}
--- md
Jamf Pro webhooks send an HTTP request to another server when an event happens, such as a computer enrolling, a
policy finishing or an API change. The request carries the names and serial numbers of devices, user names and
details of the change. Sent over plain HTTP, it can be read or altered on the way. Sent without authentication, the
receiving server cannot tell a real event from a forged one, and anything it automates on those events can be
triggered by anyone who knows its address.

This test reads every enabled webhook and fails when its address does not start with `https://` or its
authentication type is None. It never reads or shows the webhook's password, and shows only the scheme and host of
each address. Name webhooks to leave out in the `ExcludedWebhook` parameter. It supports NIST SP 800-53 SC-8
(transmission confidentiality and integrity).

#### Remediation action

1. Make sure the receiving server accepts HTTPS with a trusted certificate, and can check a user name and password
   or a header.
2. In Jamf Pro, go to **Settings** > **Global** > **Webhooks** and open each webhook this test lists.
3. Click **Edit**, change the **Webhook URL** to its `https://` address, set **Authentication Type** to **Basic
   Authentication** and enter the credentials the receiving server expects.
4. Click **Save**, and disable or delete webhooks that are no longer used.

function Test-MPJAMF1025 {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that enough Macs report no failed rule from the mSCP compliance script, through the extension attributes
    that the script, the Jamf Compliance Editor or Jamf Compliance Benchmarks write to inventory.
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id                 = 'MP.JAMF.1025',
        Title              = 'Macs pass the mSCP compliance script',
        Product            = 'Jamf Pro',
        Feature            = 'Compliance benchmarks',
        Area               = 'devices',
        ResourceType       = 'Device',
        Severity           = 'Medium',
        UserImpact         = 'Medium',
        ImplementationCost = 'Medium',
        Mitre              = 'None',
        Control            = 'nist-800-53-r5:CM-6',
        Service            = 'JAMF.JamfPro',
        Author             = 'merill'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # Lowest share of reporting Macs, in percent, that must have no failed rule.
        [ValidateRange(1, 100)]
        [int] $MinimumPercent = 90
    )

    # One row per Mac that reports a result. A count attribute ("Compliance - Failed Results Count") leaves out
    # exempt rules, so it is used when the Mac has one; otherwise the failed rules in the list attributes
    # ("Compliance - Failed Result List", "<Benchmark> - Failed Result List") are counted, where empty means none.
    # A Mac whose count attribute is empty has not run the script yet and is left out.
    $reporting = foreach ($mac in (Get-JamfProComputer)) {
        $attributes = @($mac.extensionAttributes | Where-Object { [string]$_.name -match 'Failed Results? (Count|List)' })
        $countAttributes = @($attributes | Where-Object { [string]$_.name -match 'Failed Results? Count' })
        $counts = @($countAttributes | ForEach-Object {
                $text = (@($_.values) | Where-Object { "$_".Trim() } | Select-Object -First 1)
                $number = 0
                if ($null -ne $text -and [int]::TryParse("$text".Trim(), [ref] $number)) { $number }
            })
        $lists = @($attributes | Where-Object { [string]$_.name -match 'Failed Results? List' })

        $failed = $null
        $source = $null
        if ($counts.Count -gt 0) {
            $failed = ($counts | Measure-Object -Sum).Sum
            $source = 'Failed Results Count'
        } elseif ($countAttributes.Count -eq 0 -and $lists.Count -gt 0) {
            $failed = @($lists | ForEach-Object { @($_.values) -join "`n" -split '[\r\n,;]+' } | Where-Object { $_.Trim() }).Count
            $source = 'Failed Result List'
        }
        if ($null -ne $failed) {
            [pscustomobject]@{ Name = [string]$mac.general.name; Failed = [int]$failed; Source = $source; LastContact = $mac.general.lastContact }
        }
    }

    $measure = @{
        Device         = @($reporting)
        Condition      = { $_.Failed -eq 0 }
        Describe       = { [ordered]@{ Mac = $_.Name; 'Failed rules' = $_.Failed; 'Read from' = $_.Source; 'Last contact' = $_.LastContact } }
        MinimumPercent = $MinimumPercent
        Requirement    = 'have no failed mSCP rule'
        NoDeviceReason = 'No managed Mac has a Failed Results Count or Failed Result List extension attribute. Deploy the mSCP compliance script with the Jamf Compliance Editor, or set up Jamf Compliance Benchmarks, so Macs report their results to inventory.'
    }
    Measure-JamfDevice @measure
}
--- md
The NIST macOS Security Compliance Project (mSCP) publishes security baselines for macOS, such as the CIS
benchmarks, the DISA STIG and the NIST 800-53 baselines, with a compliance script that checks each rule on the Mac.
The Jamf Compliance Editor and Jamf Compliance Benchmarks deploy that script and write the number or list of failed
rules to an extension attribute in Jamf Pro inventory. A Mac that fails rules runs with settings weaker than the
baseline the organisation chose.

This test reads the `Failed Results Count` extension attribute of each Mac, or the `Failed Result List` attribute
when there is no count, where an empty list means no rule failed. The count leaves out rules the organisation has
exempted. Macs that report neither are left out. The test passes when the share of reporting Macs with no failed
rule is at least the `MinimumPercent` parameter (90 by default). It supports NIST SP 800-53 CM-6 (configuration
settings).

#### Remediation action

1. Use the Jamf Compliance Editor to build a baseline from mSCP, then upload its configuration profiles, the
   compliance script and its extension attributes to Jamf Pro; or set up a benchmark in Jamf Compliance Benchmarks.
2. In Jamf Pro, go to **Computers** > **Smart Computer Groups** and create a group of Macs whose failed result count
   is more than 0, to find the Macs this test lists.
3. Scope the baseline's configuration profiles to those Macs, or run the compliance script with its fix option
   from a policy, and exempt rules the organisation accepts through the baseline's preference domain.
4. Raise or lower the share this test needs with the `MinimumPercent` parameter.

#### Related links

- [mSCP: macOS Security Compliance Project](https://github.com/usnistgov/macos_security)
- [Jamf Compliance Editor](https://github.com/Jamf-Concepts/jamf-compliance-editor)
- [Jamf Compliance Benchmarks: third-party compliance workflows](https://learn.jamf.com/r/en-US/jamf-compliance-benchmarks-configuration-guide/Compliance_Benchmarks_and_Third-Party_Compliance_Workflows)

function Get-JamfComplianceBenchmarkRule {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Returns one instance per rule of every Jamf Compliance Benchmark, with the rule's results across its devices.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Reads GET /compliance-benchmarks/v1/benchmarks and, for each benchmark, every page of
    GET /compliance-benchmarks/v1/benchmarks/{id}/rules through the Jamf Platform API. Rule IDs are mSCP rule IDs;
    a rule that the pack's mSCP framework file knows is mapped to it. When there is no benchmark, returns one
    instance that the test skips with how to create one.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param()

    $benchmarks = @((Invoke-JamfPlatformRequest -Path 'compliance-benchmarks/v1/benchmarks').benchmarks | Where-Object { $_ -and [string]$_.syncState -ne 'DELETING' })
    if ($benchmarks.Count -eq 0) {
        return [pscustomobject]@{ Id = 'no-benchmarks'; Title = 'Jamf Compliance Benchmarks has no benchmark'; Data = $null }
    }

    # The mSCP rules the pack's framework file knows, so an instance can name its requirement.
    $framework = Join-Path -Path $PSScriptRoot -ChildPath 'frameworks/mscp.json'
    $known = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([System.StringComparer]::Ordinal)
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $framework) {
        foreach ($id in (Get-Content -LiteralPath $framework -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).Requirements.Id) { $null = $known.Add([string]$id) }
    }

    $slugs = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)
    foreach ($benchmark in $benchmarks) {
        $title = [string]$benchmark.title
        $base = ($title.ToLowerInvariant() -replace '[^a-z0-9]+', '-').Trim('-')
        if ($base.Length -gt 40) { $base = $base.Substring(0, 40).Trim('-') }
        if (-not $base) { $base = 'benchmark' }
        # Two benchmarks with the same title still get IDs of their own.
        $slug = $base
        $n = 2
        while (-not $slugs.Add($slug)) { $slug = "$base-$n"; $n++ }

        $rules = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
        $page = 0
        do {
            $response = Invoke-JamfPlatformRequest -Path "compliance-benchmarks/v1/benchmarks/$([uri]::EscapeDataString([string]$benchmark.id))/rules?page=$page&page-size=500"
            foreach ($rule in @($response.results)) { if ($null -ne $rule) { $rules.Add($rule) } }
            $page++
        } while (@($response.results).Count -gt 0 -and $rules.Count -lt [int]$response.totalCount)

        $seen = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)
        foreach ($rule in $rules) {
            $ruleId = [string]$rule.ruleId
            $suffix = "$slug.$($ruleId -replace '[^A-Za-z0-9._-]', '-')"
            if ($suffix.Length -gt 128) { $suffix = $suffix.Substring(0, 128) }
            if (-not $seen.Add($suffix)) { continue }

            $ruleTitle = if ($rule.ruleNumber) { "$($rule.ruleNumber) $($rule.ruleTitle)" } else { [string]$rule.ruleTitle }
            $instance = [ordered]@{
                Id     = $suffix
                Title  = $ruleTitle
                Fields = @{ Benchmark = $title; Section = [string]$rule.sectionName }
                Data   = $rule
            }
            if ($known.Contains($ruleId)) { $instance.Control = "mscp:$ruleId" }
            [pscustomobject]$instance
        }
    }
}

function Test-MPJAMF2001 {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Reports each rule of the Jamf Compliance Benchmarks as a result, from the share of devices that pass it.
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id                 = 'MP.JAMF.2001',
        Title              = 'Devices pass the rules of Jamf Compliance Benchmarks',
        Product            = 'Jamf Pro',
        Feature            = 'Compliance benchmarks',
        Area               = 'devices',
        ResourceType       = 'Device',
        Severity           = 'Medium',
        UserImpact         = 'Medium',
        ImplementationCost = 'Medium',
        Mitre              = 'None',
        Control            = 'nist-800-53-r5:CM-6',
        Service            = 'JAMF.Platform',
        InstanceSource     = 'Get-JamfComplianceBenchmarkRule',
        Author             = 'merill'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # One rule of a benchmark, supplied by the engine.
        $Instance,

        # Lowest share of devices, in percent, that must pass a rule when some fail it.
        [ValidateRange(1, 100)]
        [int] $MinimumPassPercent = 100
    )

    $rule = $Instance.Data
    if ($null -eq $rule) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason 'Jamf Compliance Benchmarks has no benchmark. In Jamf Pro, go to Computers > Compliance Benchmarks, create a benchmark from an mSCP template and scope it to a smart computer group.'
        return
    }

    $devices = [int]$rule.numberOfDevices
    if ($devices -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason 'No device in the benchmark''s scope has reported a result for this rule yet.'
        return
    }

    $passed = [int]$rule.passed
    $failed = [int]$rule.failed
    $unknown = [int]$rule.unknown
    $percent = [math]::Round([double]$rule.passPercentage, 1)
    $counts = "| Passed | Failed | Unknown | Devices | Pass rate |`n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |`n| $passed | $failed | $unknown | $devices | $percent% |"

    if ($unknown -ge $devices) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "None of the $devices devices has reported whether it meets this rule. Check that the devices run macOS 15 or later and check in with Jamf Pro.`n`n$counts" -Investigate
        return $false
    }
    if ($failed -eq 0 -or $percent -ge $MinimumPassPercent) {
        $lead = if ($failed -eq 0) { "Well done. No device fails this rule." } else { "Well done. $percent% of devices pass this rule. The test needs at least $MinimumPassPercent%." }
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "$lead`n`n$counts"
        return $true
    }

    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "$failed of $devices devices fail this rule. The test needs at least $MinimumPassPercent% to pass, or no device to fail.`n`n$counts"
    $false
}
--- md
Jamf Compliance Benchmarks applies a baseline from the NIST macOS Security Compliance Project (mSCP), such as a CIS
benchmark or the DISA STIG, to a group of Macs, and reports for each rule how many devices pass, fail or have not
reported. A rule that devices fail is a setting of the baseline that is not in place on them.

This test reads every benchmark through the Jamf Platform API and gives one result per rule. A rule passes when no
device fails it, or when the share of devices that pass is at least the `MinimumPassPercent` parameter (100 by
default). A rule that no device has reported yet needs a person to look at it, and a rule with no device in scope is
skipped. A rule that the pack's mSCP framework knows is reported under that rule. It supports NIST SP 800-53 CM-6
(configuration settings).

The test needs the Jamf Platform API connection (`JAMF.Platform`), with a Jamf Account integration that has the
`compliance-benchmarks:read` scope.

#### Remediation action

1. In Jamf Pro, go to **Computers** > **Compliance Benchmarks** and open the benchmark this result names.
2. Open the rule to see which devices fail it, and why.
3. If the benchmark only monitors, switch it to enforce the rule, or deploy a configuration profile that sets it.
4. If the organisation accepts the rule's risk, remove the rule from the benchmark, or turn off this result in the
   Maester configuration.

function Measure-JamfDevice {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Counts the devices that meet a condition, and writes the result of a fleet check.

    .DESCRIPTION
    The fleet checks all have the same shape: of the devices the check applies to, what share meets the
    requirement, against the lowest share the test accepts. This writes the Markdown result (the counts and a table
    of up to MaximumListed devices that do not meet it) and returns $true when the share is high enough.

    Skips the test when no device applies, with -NoDeviceReason.

    .PARAMETER Device
    The devices the check applies to.

    .PARAMETER Condition
    A script block that gets one device as $_ and returns $true when it meets the requirement.

    .PARAMETER Describe
    A script block that gets one device that fails as $_ and returns an ordered hashtable of the columns to show.

    .PARAMETER MinimumPercent
    The lowest share of devices, in percent, that must meet the requirement.

    .PARAMETER Requirement
    The requirement in a few words, such as "have FileVault on".

    .PARAMETER Noun
    The kind of device, such as Macs.

    .PARAMETER NoDeviceReason
    Why the test is skipped when no device applies.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [AllowEmptyCollection()] [object[]] $Device,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [scriptblock] $Condition,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [scriptblock] $Describe,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [int] $MinimumPercent,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Requirement,
        [Parameter()] [string] $Noun = 'Macs',
        [Parameter()] [string] $NoDeviceReason = 'Jamf Pro manages no device this check applies to.',
        [Parameter()] [int] $MaximumListed = 50
    )

    if ($Device.Count -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason $NoDeviceReason
        return
    }

    $failing = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
    foreach ($item in $Device) {
        # Where-Object runs the condition with $_ set to the device.
        if (-not @($item | Where-Object -FilterScript $Condition)) { $failing.Add($item) }
    }
    $meeting = $Device.Count - $failing.Count
    $percent = [math]::Floor(100 * $meeting / $Device.Count * 10) / 10
    $passed = $percent -ge $MinimumPercent

    $summary = "$meeting of $($Device.Count) $Noun ($percent%) $Requirement. The test needs at least $MinimumPercent%."
    $result = if ($passed -and $failing.Count -eq 0) { "Well done. All $($Device.Count) $Noun $Requirement." }
    elseif ($passed) { "Well done. $summary" }
    else { $summary }

    if ($failing.Count -gt 0) {
        $rows = @($failing | Select-Object -First $MaximumListed | ForEach-Object -Process $Describe | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject]$_ })
        $result += "`n`n$(ConvertTo-JamfMarkdownTable -InputObject $rows)"
        if ($failing.Count -gt $MaximumListed) { $result += "`n`nAnd $($failing.Count - $MaximumListed) more." }
    }
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $result
    $passed
}
function Get-JamfProPagedResult {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Reads every page of a Jamf Pro API list (one that answers with totalCount and results) and returns the results.

    .PARAMETER Path
    The list's path, such as 'api/v3/computer-prestages'.

    .PARAMETER Query
    More query parameters, already encoded, such as 'section=GENERAL&section=SECURITY'.

    .PARAMETER PageSize
    Results per page. Jamf Pro allows up to 2000 on most lists.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([object[]])]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Path,
        [Parameter()] [string] $Query,
        [Parameter()] [ValidateRange(1, 2000)] [int] $PageSize = 500
    )

    $state = Get-MtConnectionState -Service 'JAMF.JamfPro'
    $cacheKey = "paged:$Path`?$Query"
    if ($state -and $state.Cache.ContainsKey($cacheKey)) { return $state.Cache[$cacheKey] }

    $results = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
    $page = 0
    do {
        $parts = @("page=$page", "page-size=$PageSize")
        if ($Query) { $parts += $Query }
        $response = Invoke-JamfProRequest -Path "$($Path.TrimStart('/'))?$($parts -join '&')" -NoCache
        foreach ($item in @($response.results)) { if ($null -ne $item) { $results.Add($item) } }
        $total = [int]$response.totalCount
        $page++
    } while (@($response.results).Count -gt 0 -and $results.Count -lt $total)

    $array = $results.ToArray()
    if ($state) { $state.Cache[$cacheKey] = $array }
    $array
}
function Invoke-JamfPlatformRequest {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Reads one Jamf Platform API path through the connection, from the run's cache when it was read before.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Sends the X-Environment-Id header the Platform API needs on every request. A 401 answer gets a new token once
    and tries again.

    .PARAMETER Path
    The path and query, relative to the regional gateway, such as 'compliance-benchmarks/v1/benchmarks'.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([object])]
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Path)

    $state = Get-MtConnectionState -Service 'JAMF.Platform'
    if (-not $state -or -not $state.Token) { throw 'The Jamf Platform API is not connected. Run Connect-Maester -Service JAMF.Platform.' }
    $key = $Path.TrimStart('/')
    if ($state.Cache.ContainsKey($key)) { return $state.Cache[$key] }

    $uri = [uri]::new($state.Server, $key)
    $response = $null
    foreach ($attempt in 1, 2) {
        try {
            $response = Invoke-JamfHttp -Uri $uri -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $($state.Token)"; 'X-Environment-Id' = $state.EnvironmentId; Accept = 'application/json' }
            break
        } catch {
            # A token can expire or be revoked during a long run: get a new one once and try again.
            if ($attempt -eq 1 -and [int]($_.Exception.Response.StatusCode) -eq 401) { Update-JamfPlatformToken -State $state; continue }
            throw (New-JamfRequestError -ErrorRecord $_ -Path $key)
        }
    }
    $state.Cache[$key] = $response
    $response
}
function Get-JamfProComputer {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Returns the inventory of every managed Mac, with the sections the fleet checks read.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Reads GET /api/v4/computers-inventory once per run with the GENERAL, OPERATING_SYSTEM, DISK_ENCRYPTION, SECURITY
    and EXTENSION_ATTRIBUTES sections, filtered to Macs that Jamf Pro manages. Falls back to /api/v3 on a server
    that has no v4. Needs the Read Computers privilege.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([object[]])]
    param()

    $query = 'section=GENERAL&section=OPERATING_SYSTEM&section=DISK_ENCRYPTION&section=SECURITY&section=EXTENSION_ATTRIBUTES&filter=general.remoteManagement.managed%3D%3Dtrue'
    try {
        Get-JamfProPagedResult -Path 'api/v4/computers-inventory' -Query $query
    } catch {
        if ($_.FullyQualifiedErrorId -notlike 'JamfRequest404*') { throw }
        Get-JamfProPagedResult -Path 'api/v3/computers-inventory' -Query $query
    }
}

## 8. Automated Device Enrollment (ADE) instances and prestages

### ADE instances

- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/v1/device-enrollments`
- **Privilege:** **Read Device Enrollment Program Instances** (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-device-enrollments.md; [PD])

- **Sync state:** `/v1/device-enrollments/syncs` and `/v1/device-enrollments/{id}/syncs/latest`, same privilege [PD]

### Computer prestages

- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/v3/computer-prestages`
- **Privilege:** **Read Computer PreStage Enrollments** (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v3-computer-prestages.md; [PD])
- **Parameters:** `page`, `page-size`, `sort` (default `id:desc`); no filter
- **Fields:**
  - booleans: `mandatory`, `mdmRemovable`, `requireAuthentication`, `preventActivationLock`, `enableDeviceBasedActivationLock`, `autoAdvanceSetup`, `defaultPrestage`, `keepExistingSiteMembership`, `keepExistingLocationInformation`, `installProfilesDuringSetup`, `enableRecoveryLock`, `rotateRecoveryLockPassword`, `pssoEnabled`
  - strings: `displayName`, `authenticationPrompt`, `deviceEnrollmentProgramInstanceId`, `enrollmentSiteId`, `siteId`, `profileUuid`
  - `skipSetupItems`: object
  - `recoveryLockPasswordType`: enum `MANUAL`, `RANDOM`
  - `prestageMinimumOsTargetVersionType`: enum `NO_ENFORCEMENT`, `MINIMUM_OS_LATEST_VERSION`, `MINIMUM_OS_LATEST_MAJOR_VERSION`, `MINIMUM_OS_LATEST_MINOR_VERSION`, `MINIMUM_OS_SPECIFIC_VERSION`, plus `minimumOsSpecificVersion`

## Families: one test, several results

Some checks produce one result per item: per drift folder, per recommendation, per user. Declare
`InstanceSource` with the name of a function in the same file. The engine calls that function when the test
runs (never during discovery) and runs the test once per object it returns, passing the object as `$Instance`.

```powershell
function Get-ContosoAdminUnit {
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param()
    foreach ($unit in Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'directory/administrativeUnits') {
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Id    = $unit.id                     # required: the instance suffix
            Title = "Administrative unit '$($unit.displayName)' is restricted"   # optional
            Data  = $unit                        # optional: anything the test needs
        }
    }
}

function Test-ContosoAdminUnitRestricted {
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'CONTOSO.2001',
        Title = 'Administrative units are restricted.',
        Severity = 'Medium',
        Service = 'Graph',
        InstanceSource = 'Get-ContosoAdminUnit'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # The administrative unit to check, supplied by the engine.
        $Instance
    )

    $restricted = [bool]$Instance.Data.isMemberManagementRestricted
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "Member management restricted: $restricted"
    return $restricted
}
```

The instance object has:

| Property | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Id` | Yes | The suffix. The row's ID is `<parent ID>.<Id>`, for example `CONTOSO.2001.4f6c...`. It must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$` and be unique within the family. |
| `Title` | No | The instance's title. Defaults to `-TestTitle` from the helper, then the attribute's title. |
| `Severity` | No | The instance's severity, used when the config sets none. |
| `Tag` | No | Extra tags written to the instance's row. |
| `Fields` | No | Facts about the instance that a report can group or filter by, as a hashtable of names to strings or arrays of strings, for example `@{ Pillar = 'Identity'; Category = 'Access control' }`. Written to the row's `Fields`; other values are left out. |
| `Product`, `Feature`, `Area`, `RelatedProduct`, `UserImpact`, `ImplementationCost`, `Mitre` | No | What this instance is about, when that differs from its family, with the same keys as the attribute. A family that reads results from another tool, such as the Zero Trust Assessment pack, places each result under its own product this way. A value the taxonomy does not know is left out, and the row keeps the family's. |
| `Control` | No | The requirements this instance implements, as one `<framework-key>:<requirement-id>` value or a list, for example `'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1'`. They replace the family's `Control`, and the row gets its own `Benchmark` and the requirements' `Related` references, as a test does (see [What the result gets](#what-the-result-gets)). A family that reads another tool's results per policy, such as the ScubaGear pack, maps each result to its requirement this way. A value that is not written `<framework-key>:<id>`, or that names a requirement the framework file does not have, is left out; when none is left, the row keeps the family's `Control` and `Benchmark`. |

Each instance row carries `ParentId` (the family's ID) and `InstanceId`. When the family does not produce
instance rows, the result has one row on the parent ID instead:

| What happened | Row on the parent ID |

288 attribute-rubric.md
---
title: Attribute rubric
description: How to choose the classification, priority and mapping attributes of a Maester test, and how those choices are checked.
sidebar:
  order: 2
---

# Attribute rubric

Every test shipped with Maester declares what it is about, how urgent a failure is and which attack techniques
it addresses. This page is the rule book for those values. Unit tests check what can be checked mechanically, and
a review step checks the judgement calls against this page. A custom test may use the same attributes; the rules
apply to it only if you want them to.

The [test builder](/test-builder) lets you pick the values with this guidance beside each field and
shows the code as you go.

| Question | Attributes | Required for built-in tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What is it about? | `Product`, `RelatedProduct`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType` | All except `RelatedProduct` |
| What do I fix first? | `Severity`, `UserImpact`, `ImplementationCost` | `Severity` always. The other two unless `Severity` is `Info` |
| What does it map to? | `Mitre`, `Control` | `Mitre` (technique IDs or `None`) |
| Is it current? | `Lifecycle`, `ReplacedBy` | No. `Lifecycle` defaults to `Stable` |

The allowed keys for `Product`, `Feature`, `Area` and `ResourceType` are in
[`powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1`](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1).
Add a key there in the same pull request as the first test that needs it.

## Rate the test, not your tenant

Rate every value for a typical organization that fails the test, using the fix the test's own Markdown file
recommends. Do not rate for the best case, the worst case or one tenant you know. When two values fit, choose the
lower one for `Severity`, `UserImpact` and `ImplementationCost`. A reader should be able to see the reason for
each value in the test's description and remediation text.

## Product

The product where the fix is made. One value.

- Use the product whose admin surface holds the setting, not every product the test reads from.
- Tests in a product folder (`tests/maester/entra`, `tests/cisa/exchange`) use that folder's product.
- A product the test only reads from, or a licence it needs, is not a second product. `Service` and `License`
  already say that.

## RelatedProduct

Other products the test also checks or depends on. Optional list, never the same key as `Product`.

- Add one when an admin of that product would expect to find the test under it. An Exchange Online test about an
  anti-phishing policy that is managed in the Defender portal has `RelatedProduct = 'defender'`.
- Add one when the fix is made in that product's portal although the test lives in another product's folder.
- Do not add a product only because its API is called.

## Feature

The part of the product the test is about. One key from the product's `Features` list.

- Choose the feature whose settings page or object type the remediation sends the admin to.
- When a test spans two features, choose the one that fails most directly. A Conditional Access policy that
  requires a compliant device is `conditional-access`, not `devices`.
- Tests that check the same thing get the same feature, whatever folder or suite they are in.
- A feature that would hold one test only is usually too narrow. Prefer an existing feature.

## Area

The security theme, whatever the product. One key.

| Key | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `authentication` | How an identity proves who it is: MFA, authentication methods, passwords, legacy protocols, Kerberos and NTLM hardening, session and token lifetime. |
| `privileged-access` | Administrative roles and accounts: who holds them, just-in-time elevation, emergency access, admin tiering, delegated admin rights. |
| `access-control` | Who may reach which resource under which conditions: device, location and risk conditions, permissions on objects, user defaults. |
| `applications` | App registrations, service principals and their credentials, consent and API permissions, OAuth apps, add-ins, connectors. |
| `external-access` | Guests, cross-tenant access, federation and trusts, external sharing and external communication. |
| `devices` | Device compliance, enrollment and configuration, endpoint protection, device identity. |
| `email-protection` | Anti-phishing, anti-spam and anti-malware, Safe Links and Safe Attachments, SPF, DKIM and DMARC, mail flow rules, meeting and messaging protections. |
| `data-protection` | Data loss prevention, sensitivity labels, encryption, retention, backup. |
| `logging-and-detection` | Audit logs, diagnostic settings, alert policies, sensors and the health of detection tooling. |
| `identity-lifecycle` | Stale and dormant accounts, ownership, access reviews, entitlement management, group membership hygiene. |
| `infrastructure` | The directory and platform itself: domain controllers, DNS, replication, sites, schema, Group Policy health, protocol hardening, subscriptions, tenant-wide platform settings. |
| `engineering-systems` | DevOps organizations, repositories, pipelines, build identities, the software supply chain. |
| `ai` | AI agents and copilots: who can use and share them, how they authenticate, what data and tools they reach. |

When more than one area fits, choose by what the control is for, in this order:

1. It protects administrators or admin rights: `privileged-access`.
2. It decides how sign-in is proven: `authentication`.
3. It is about an application, service principal or agent as the subject: `applications`, or `ai` for agents.
4. It is about people or data outside the organization: `external-access`.
5. Otherwise the area that names the mechanism: `access-control`, `devices`, `email-protection`,
   `data-protection`, `logging-and-detection`, `identity-lifecycle`, `engineering-systems`, `infrastructure`.

A product never decides the area on its own. An Azure DevOps test about who is a Project Collection Administrator
is `privileged-access`, not `engineering-systems`.

Inventory and health tests with no security theme of their own are `infrastructure`. When no area fits, choose
the closest and say so in the pull request, so the list can be reviewed.

## ResourceType

What a failing result points at. One key.

- `Tenant` when the test evaluates one tenant-, organization-, forest- or domain-wide setting. The result is
  about the environment.
- `Tenant` when the test checks that at least one policy of a kind exists, even when it lists the policies that
  satisfy it. A failing result has nothing to list.
- `Tenant` when the test evaluates the single default or global policy of a kind, because there is one of it and
  it applies to everyone.
- Otherwise the kind of object a failing result lists or counts: `User`, `Application`, `Device`,
  `ConditionalAccessPolicy`, `GroupPolicy` and so on. A test that evaluates every policy and lists the ones that
  fail uses the policy type.
- A test that counts objects for review (an inventory test) uses the type it counts. When no key names that kind
  of object and it is a one-off, use `Tenant`.
- A family test, which yields one result per instance, uses the type of the instance.

## Severity

The risk to the organization while the test fails. Not the effort to fix it and not the disruption of fixing it.

| Value | A failing result means |
| --- | --- |
| `Critical` | An attacker with no special position can take over the tenant, the domain or a privileged identity, or a secret is already exposed. Directly exploitable and wide in reach. |
| `High` | A primary control is missing or weakened for many users or for privileged identities, and common techniques such as phishing, password spray or consent phishing are enough to use it. |
| `Medium` | A defence-in-depth control is missing, or the exposure is limited to a few objects or one workload, or using it needs another weakness first. |
| `Low` | Hardening or hygiene with a small security effect on its own. |
| `Info` | The test reports a fact for review and makes no risk judgement. Info tests are left out of scores. |

Decide in this order:

1. **Reach.** Privileged identities or the whole tenant move the value up. A single workload or a few objects
   move it down.
2. **Directness.** Usable from the internet or by any signed-in user moves it up. Needing an earlier compromise
   moves it down. A password taken by phishing, spray or stuffing is not an earlier compromise: those are the
   common techniques `High` already assumes.
3. **Role of the control.** The main control for a threat rates higher than a second layer behind another control.

`Critical` is rare. If the description cannot say in one sentence how an attacker gets from the failing state to
admin rights or exposed secrets, the value is `High` or lower. A benchmark's own wording does not set the value:
a SHALL policy can be `Medium`.

Five cases come up often:

- **A test that passes whenever its data can be read** is `Info`, whatever the data is about. If the fact
  deserves a severity, the test should fail on it.
- **A failure that is only an outage or untidiness**, such as replication health, an expiring token or an unused
  object, is `Low`. It is `Medium` or higher only when the outage switches off a security control, and then it is
  rated as the loss of that control.
- **Alerts and notifications** are a second layer behind the control they watch, so they are `Medium` at most.
- **The same check in two suites** gets the same value in both. Usually the second is a shim that returns the
  first test's result and declares all of its values; see
  [Tests that another suite already has](./index.mdx#tests-that-another-suite-already-has).
- **The main control against an attack that starts from a stolen password** is `High`. A second layer behind
  that control is `Medium`. Number matching against MFA fatigue is `High`; showing the app name and location in
  the prompt is `Medium`.

Anchors from existing tests:

| Test | Value | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No Group Policy object contains a `cpassword` | `Critical` | Any domain user can read and decrypt the stored password. |
| No domain admin account has a service principal name | `Critical` | Any domain user can request a ticket and crack an admin password offline. |
| Legacy authentication is blocked | `High` | Password spray bypasses MFA for every user. |
| Number matching is required for Authenticator push notifications | `High` | MFA fatigue works against any user once a password is phished. |
| Authenticator shows the app name and location | `Medium` | A second layer behind number matching. |
| Users cannot register applications | `Medium` | Needs a signed-in user and a further step to cause harm. |
| MailTips are enabled for end users | `Low` | A small aid against mis-sent mail. |
| Disabled user count should be retrievable | `Info` | Inventory for review. |
| [EIDSCA.AP14 — users may read other users](/docs/tests/EIDSCA.AP14) | `Info` | Disabling `allowedToReadOtherUsers` is not itself a security finding. Review the restriction because it can disrupt collaboration, user lookup and default features. |

Microsoft's [Zero Trust Assessment](https://github.com/microsoft/zerotrustassessment) rates many of the same
Microsoft Entra and Intune settings. Where it has a test for the same setting, compare your value with its risk
level and give the reason in the pull request if the two differ.

## UserImpact

How much the recommended fix disrupts end users. Administrators and the owners of applications are not end
users here. Developers are the end users of Azure DevOps and GitHub.

| Value | Applying the fix |
| --- | --- |
| `Low` | End users notice nothing, or only administrators are affected. |
| `Medium` | Some users change how they work or meet a new prompt: a group loses a capability, users register a method once, a legacy client stops working for a subset. |
| `High` | Most users change a daily habit, or a mistake locks people out or stops mail or an app for many. Needs communication and a staged rollout. |

Omit `UserImpact` when `Severity` is `Info`.

## ImplementationCost

How much administrator work the recommended fix takes.

| Value | The fix is |
| --- | --- |
| `Low` | One setting or one policy in one portal. Under an hour, with no dependency on another team, a licence purchase or a rollout. |
| `Medium` | Several steps: a policy that needs exclusions and a pilot, clean-up of a handful of objects, coordination with one other team. Hours to a few days. |
| `High` | A project: new licences, infrastructure or process, a migration of users or apps, or clean-up across many objects. Weeks or more. |

Clean-up that one administrator can finish alone in a sitting is `Low`. Clean-up that needs the owner of each
object is `Medium`. Turning on a plan that is billed by use is `Medium`: the click is easy, the budget approval is
not. Count the work of the fix, including exclusions and rollout, but not the time to decide.

Omit `ImplementationCost` when `Severity` is `Info`.

## Mitre

The MITRE ATT&CK techniques that the checked control prevents or detects. A list of technique IDs, or `None`.

- IDs only, in the form `T1110` or `T1110.003`. Tactic names are looked up from the pinned ATT&CK release
  (`powershell/assets/MaesterAttackTechniques.json`) and are never typed.
- Use a sub-technique when the control addresses only that sub-technique. When three or more sub-techniques of
  one technique apply, list the technique instead. Do not list a technique together with one of its own
  sub-techniques.
- List a technique only if the test's description explains, or plainly implies, how the control stops or reveals
  it. At most five.
- A test that implements a benchmark which publishes a mapping, such as CISA SCuBA, starts from that mapping and
  then applies these rules. An ID the pinned release has retired is replaced by its successor in that release,
  found by name.
- The description means the comment-based help and the Markdown file together.
- Use `None` for a test with no attacker behaviour behind it, such as replication health or an inventory count.
  An inventory test lists a technique only when the fact it reports is itself the precondition of that technique,
  such as accounts that do not require Kerberos pre-authentication.
- A retired or unknown ID fails the unit tests.

## Control

Requirements of frameworks the test implements or supports, written `<framework-key>:<requirement-id>`, for
example `cis-m365:5.1.5.1`, `cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1` or `nist-800-53-r5:IA-2(1)`. Optional list. Any test can use
it: one shipped with Maester or one of your own.

- `Control` is the only way a test is mapped to a framework. A CIS test carries `Control = 'cis-m365:5.1.5.1'` and
  a CISA test carries `Control = 'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1'` and an ASD test `Control = 'essential-eight:ISM-1504'`.
  Every test in `tests/cis`, `tests/cisa` and `tests/asd` must name a requirement of its suite's framework. The unit
  tests check this.
- The first value that names a requirement in a framework file becomes the `Benchmark` of the result. Put the
  requirement the test is written for first, and any other requirement it supports after it.
- Use the same attribute for a test that exists for its own reasons and also supports a requirement: a Maester
  test that checks the setting a CISA policy asks for, or a CIS test that also supports a NIST control.
- When the key is a framework shipped with Maester (`cis-m365`, `cis-github`, `cisa-scuba`, `essential-eight`, `ism`), the requirement must
  exist in that framework's file. If it is new, add it to the file with its facts. The module build and the unit
  tests fail otherwise.
- Do not repeat the `Related` controls of a requirement. The framework file lists them and Maester adds them to
  the result.
- List a requirement only when a passing result is evidence for it. A test that checks one part of a requirement
  may list it; a test that is merely on the same topic may not.

A reference says the test supports the requirement. It never says the organization complies with it.

### NIST SP 800-53

A test may list the NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls its setting implements, as `nist-800-53-r5:<control>`.

- Use an ID from the pinned list, [`powershell/assets/MaesterNistControls.json`](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/powershell/assets/MaesterNistControls.json):
  a base control (`AC-2`) or an enhancement (`IA-2(1)`). The unit tests reject anything else.
- List a control only when a passing result is direct evidence that it is implemented for what the test checks.
- Prefer the enhancement when the test checks exactly what it says: MFA for privileged accounts is `IA-2(1)`.
  Do not list a base control together with one of its own enhancements.
- At most three, best fit first. Never the policy-and-procedures controls (`AC-1`, `IA-1` and so on).
- A test that only reports a count, or checks health, licensing or tidiness, lists none, unless the count is
  itself what a control asks to be tracked: dormant accounts for `AC-2(3)`.
- A test that implements a CISA SCuBA policy does not list NIST controls. CISA publishes that mapping, the
  framework file carries it as `Related`, and the result gets it from there.

## Lifecycle and ReplacedBy

- `Preview`: new and still changing. Not run unless previews are included.
- `Stable`: the default.
- `Deprecated`: kept so history stays readable. Give `ReplacedBy` when another test took its place.

## Tag

`Tag` holds labels the owner of a test folder finds useful. It is not part of Maester's taxonomy.

- Built-in tests do not carry tags for product, feature, area, suite, benchmark, licence, severity or their own ID.
  Each of those has an attribute or is derived.
- A custom test may tag freely.

## How the rubric is enforced

1. **Unit tests** (`powershell/tests/general/NativeTestAttributes.Tests.ps1`) fail when a built-in test misses a
   required attribute, uses a key that is not in the taxonomy, pairs a feature with the wrong product, lists a
   retired ATT&CK technique, carries a taxonomy tag, names a requirement that a shipped framework file does not
   have, or is a CIS or CISA test without a `Control` for its own framework.
2. **Attribute review** runs on every pull request that adds a test or changes one of these attributes. A
   reviewer model reads the test, its Markdown file and this page, and fails the check when a value does not fit
   the rubric, with the value it expected and the reason. It also sees the attributes of the other tests with the
   same product and feature. It fails a test whose area, resource type or severity differs from the same check in
   another suite, and whose user impact or implementation cost differs when both plainly recommend the same fix.
   MITRE techniques and related products are not compared. A maintainer can overrule it.
3. **Reviewers**, human or agent, apply the same page. See `AGENTS.md`.

Jamf Compliance Editor User Guide Page of 25 48
￼
￼
Uploaded Items
When using the “Jamf Pro Upload” button the following actions are performed:
1. A category is created in Jamf Pro with the name of the <Operating
System>_<baseline>, for example, “Ventura_cis_lvl1”
2. Generated profiles are uploaded to Jamf Pro and labeled with the category
3. The compliance script is uploaded to Jamf Pro and labeled with the category
4. Four Extension Attributes are created:
a. Compliance
-
Exemptions
b. Compliance
-
Failed Result List
c. Compliance
-
Failed Results Count
d. Compliance
-
Version
Note: Jamf Compliance Editor 1.2 and later allows you to choose what to upload to
Jamf Pro.
Jamf Compliance Editor User Guide Page of 26 48
￼
￼
Scoping Content
The Configuration Profiles and Compliance script which are uploaded via the “Jamf Pro
Upload” button will be un-scoped. Take the opportunity to inspect them before starting
any test deployments.
Jamf Compliance Editor User Guide Page of 35 48
￼
Extension Attributes
Once the configuration profiles and scripts are scoped, the included Extension
Attributes (EA) can be used to measure an organization’s state of compliance.
Compliance
-
Exemptions
The custom JSON schema which needs to be manually uploaded to Jamf Pro can be
used to determine any exemptions that an organization needs when calculating
compliance. When using the custom schema, the exemptions are written to /Library/
Managed Preferences/org.<baseline>.audit.plist. This EA will display which exemptions
are in place on a given system.
Compliance
-
Failed Result List
The failed result list EA displays which rules in a given baseline/benchmark are not
being met. One thing to note, rules that are exempt will still show up in this list. Being
exempt from a rule is still considered a finding and needs to be reported.
Compliance
-
Failed Results Count
The failed results count EA calculates what rules are being met, but also calculates
exemptions. Exemptions are not counted towards the total results count. For example,
if a system failed five rules, but had an exemption in place for two rules, the EA would
be three. This EA is used for calculating membership to the smart group used for
remediation policy.
Compliance
-
Version
The version EA displays which version of the compliance script is currently auditing a

Review of the enrollment group is finished. I made seven fixes, listed below. All eight checks pass `Get-MtTest -Path` as valid with no errors or warnings. The whole `./spec` run passes 126 of 126, which includes `Pack.Tests.ps1` (validity, framework mapping and the `Test-MtPack` scan) and every group's spec.

**What I changed and why**

1. **MP.JAMF.1025, logic.** A Mac whose `Compliance - Version` attribute is empty is now left out. The Jamf Compliance Editor guide says this attribute shows the version of the compliance script auditing the Mac, so an empty value means the script never ran. Before, such a Mac could count as compliant because its count or list read 0 or empty.
2. **MP.JAMF.1025, guide.** The .md now says that Macs with an empty `Compliance - Version` are left out. It also says that an empty failed-result list cannot tell a Mac that passes every rule from a Mac outside the baseline's scope, and points to MP.JAMF.2001 for Jamf Compliance Benchmarks.
3. **MP.JAMF.1012, Control.** I dropped `nist-800-53-r5:CM-8` and kept only `AC-19`. The rubric lists a NIST control only when a passing result is direct evidence for it, and having user-initiated enrollment off says nothing about the component inventory. I updated the .md to match.
4. **MP.JAMF.1016, Control.** I removed `nist-800-53-r5:CM-8`. The rubric says a health check lists no NIST control, and token expiry is a health check. The .md now also says the test fails when Jamf Pro shows an expiry date it cannot read, which the code already did.
5. **MP.JAMF.1016, Severity.** I kept Medium. The rubric's rule is that an expiring token is Low unless the outage switches off a security control. Here it does: new devices skip the PreStage's mandatory MDM profile, supervision and sign-in, and the .md explains that.
6. **MP.JAMF.1017, guide.** I removed "or a header" from step 1. The research gives only two values for `authentication_type`: `NONE` and `BASIC`.
7. **`spec/Enrollment.Tests.ps1`:**
   - The fixture script blocks called with `&` (`$script:Webhook`, `$script:Token`, `$script:Platform`) are now functions (`New-JamfSpecWebhook`, `New-JamfSpecToken`, `New-JamfSpecPlatform`), to follow the pack's rule against invoking script blocks.
   - I added two tests: 1016 fails on an expiry date it cannot read, and 1025 leaves out a Mac whose `Compliance - Version` is empty.

**Checked and found correct (no change needed)**
- **Endpoints and fields:** every endpoint, field and enum is confirmed in `pro-api.md`, `benchmarks.md` and the reference pages, including the paging and `syncState` values. The Classic webhook schema declares `enabled` as a boolean; the check also accepts the string "true".
- **Code:** single results are always wrapped in `@()`, there is no stray output, no connection checks, no outer try/catch and no `&` in pack files. The webhook password and the address path are never shown.
- **2001 instance IDs:** they match the engine's pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$`, and an instance's `Control` is set only for rules that `mscp.json` contains.
- **Other attributes:** Area, ResourceType, UserImpact, ImplementationCost and Mitre fit the rubric. All Mitre IDs are in the pinned ATT&CK release, and T1685 is the right replacement for the retired T1562.001.

**Still uncertain**
- **No safe way to read benchmark lists in 1025.** For the "<Benchmark> - Failed Result List" attributes, nothing in the inventory tells a clean Mac from one outside the benchmark's scope, so those Macs can still raise the pass rate. Whether Jamf leaves `values` empty for Macs that were never scoped is not documented. This is now stated in the .md.
- **Unconfirmed formats:** the value format of the failed-result list attributes, and the format of `tokenExpirationDate` beyond the reference example `2000-10-30`.
- **Unconfirmed `passPercentage` scale:** the reference example is 75, so a 0 to 100 scale is assumed.
- **Names in the guides not checked against live Jamf pages:**
  - the UI paths **Settings > Global > Webhooks**, **Settings > Global > User-initiated enrollment** and **Settings > Global > Automated Device Enrollment**, and **Computers > Compliance Benchmarks**;
  - the PreStage checkbox labels;
  - the learn.jamf.com page names.
- **Not run live:** nothing was checked against a real Jamf Pro server or the Platform API.

**Helpers added:** none.
